$comment: What is the author's own in a Kotlin value written into HTML, judged by both editors alike: a const val of the file or the workspace, reached through its object, an enum entry, a dollar written as a template, a literal repeated, a nested template of literals; and what is not, a val that is not const, a property in capitals. A case may give `constants`, the workspace's const val names.

cases.name: a nested template whose holes are literals is the author's own
a dollar written as a template is the author's own in a DSL expression
cases.source:
import io.github.markusaugust.streamlord.html.*
fun f() = elements { div { dataText("${"$"}count") } }

cases.name: a dollar written as a template is the author's own in an HTML string

issues.message: Kotlin writes $q into the HTML as it is. If it can hold text from outside, build the string with interpolate(...), which escapes it; if it is markup you built, declare it Html or wrap it in Trusted(...).
fixes:
import io.github.markusaugust.streamlord.core.domain.interpolate fun f(q: String) = interpolate("

%s

", q).text

cases.name: a const val of an object in the file, reached through the object
a workspace const val reached through its object
cases.source:
import io.github.markusaugust.streamlord.html.*
fun f() = elements { div { dataOnClick("@post('${Routes.SAVE}')") } }

cases.name: a const val of the file in camel case, reached through its object
a val of an object that is not const is not the author's own

issues.message: Kotlin writes ${Routes.save} into data-on, which Datastar runs as an expression or follows as a signal path. Text from outside becomes code there, even inside quotes. Put the value in an attribute of its own, such as data-label, and read it in the expression with el.dataset.label; only a number or a boolean is safe to write in.

cases.name: an enum entry is the author's own

issues.message: Kotlin interpolates $tab here; the browser will never see a signal. Write signal("tab"), make the literal $$"..." (Kotlin 2.2+), or escape as ${'$'}tab.

cases.name: an enum entry of Streamlord's is the author's own, as in HtmlDslTest
cases.source:
import io.github.markusaugust.streamlord.html.*
fun f() = elements { div { dataOnFetch("evt.detail.type === '${FetchEventType.STARTED}' && (${set("busy", true)})") { window = true } } }

cases.name: a property of a parameter in capitals is not a constant
cases.source:
import io.github.markusaugust.streamlord.html.*
fun f(req: R) = elements { div { dataOnClick("@post('${req.SAVE}')") } }

issues.message: Kotlin writes ${req.SAVE} into data-on, which Datastar runs as an expression or follows as a signal path. Text from outside becomes code there, even inside quotes. Put the value in an attribute of its own, such as data-label, and read it in the expression with el.dataset.label; only a number or a boolean is safe to write in.

cases.name: a literal repeated a number of times is the author's own
a String repeated is not the author's own

issues.message: Kotlin writes ${q.repeat(2)} into data-text, which Datastar runs as an expression or follows as a signal path. Text from outside becomes code there, even inside quotes. Put the value in an attribute of its own, such as data-label, and read it in the expression with el.dataset.label; only a number or a boolean is safe to write in.
